# `silk/time/plain_date`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Calendar dates without a time or a time zone: the [`PlainDate`](#PlainDate) type and [`Weekday`](#Weekday).

## When to use

Use [`PlainDate`](#PlainDate) for a day that means the same thing everywhere, such as a birthday, a due
date, or a date in a file. It is not a point in time: the same date starts at different
instants in different time zones. For a point in time, use `silk.time.instant`.

## Details

Dates are in the ISO 8601 calendar, which applies the Gregorian leap year rule to every year.
The range is `-271821-04-19` to `+275760-09-13`, the range of ECMAScript Temporal. Values are
always valid dates: a `PlainDate` cannot hold February 30.

## Examples

### Parse a date, move it, and print it

```silk
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.time.plain_date { PlainDate, Weekday }
import silk.time.text { TimeParseError }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  match PlainDate.parse("2026-11-19") {
    Result<PlainDate, TimeParseError>.Success { value } => {
      let later = value.addDays(45)
      if later.year() != 2027 || later.month() != 1 || later.day() != 3 {
        return 1
      }
      if value.daysUntil(later) != 45 {
        return 2
      }
      match value.weekday() {
        Weekday.Thursday => {
          return 0
        }
        _ => {
          return 3
        }
      }
    }
    Result<PlainDate, TimeParseError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 4
    }
  }
}
```

Import as `PlainDate` with `import silk.time.plain_date { PlainDate }`.

<a id="PlainDate"></a>

## `PlainDate`

```silk
pub struct PlainDate
```

A calendar date in the ISO 8601 calendar: a year, a month, and a day, with no time and no time
zone.

### Details

A value is always a date that exists, from `-271821-04-19` to `+275760-09-13`. Year 0 is the
year before year 1. `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, and `>=` compare dates in calendar order.
`Display` writes `YYYY-MM-DD`, with a sign and six digits for a year outside 0 to 9999.

<a id="PlainDate.impl.weekOfYear"></a>

### Method `weekOfYear`

```silk
pub fn weekOfYear(self: Self) -> u8
```

Returns the ISO 8601 week number of the date, from 1 to 53.

#### Details

Weeks start on Monday, and week 1 is the week with the first Thursday of the year. So the
first days of January can be in week 52 or 53 of the year before, and the last days of
December can be in week 1 of the next year. [`PlainDate.yearOfWeek`](#PlainDate.impl.yearOfWeek) gives the year that the
week belongs to.

<a id="PlainDate.impl.yearOfWeek"></a>

### Method `yearOfWeek`

```silk
pub fn yearOfWeek(self: Self) -> i32
```

Returns the year that the ISO 8601 week of the date belongs to.

#### Details

It differs from [`PlainDate.year`](#PlainDate.impl.year) for the days of January in the last week of the year
before, and the days of December in week 1 of the next year. `2027-01-01` is in week 53 of
2026.

<a id="PlainDate.impl.checkedAddPeriod"></a>

### Method `checkedAddPeriod`

```silk
pub fn checkedAddPeriod(self: Self, period: Period, overflow: Overflow) -> Option<PlainDate>
```

Returns the date that `period` leads to from this date, or `None` when it is outside the
range, or when `overflow` is `Reject` and the day does not exist in the month reached.

#### Details

The years and months are added first. If the month reached has no such day, as for one
month after January 31, `Overflow.Constrain` uses the last day of that month. Then the
weeks and days are added, with the whole days of the time part of the period; the rest of
the time part is dropped. This is the rule of ECMAScript Temporal.

#### Gotchas

The order matters, so adding and then subtracting the same period does not always return
the first date: January 31 plus one month is the end of February, and one month before
that is January 28 or 29.

<a id="PlainDate.impl.addPeriod"></a>

### Method `addPeriod`

```silk
pub fn addPeriod(self: Self, period: Period) -> PlainDate
```

Returns the date that `period` leads to from this date, with a day that does not exist in
the month reached replaced by the last day of that month.

#### Details

The rule is the one of [`PlainDate.checkedAddPeriod`](#PlainDate.impl.checkedAddPeriod) with `Overflow.Constrain`. To go
back, add `period.negate()`.

#### Gotchas

A result outside the range traps. [`PlainDate.checkedAddPeriod`](#PlainDate.impl.checkedAddPeriod) returns `None` instead.

<a id="PlainDate.impl.checkedAddParts"></a>

### Method `checkedAddParts`

```silk
pub fn checkedAddParts(self: Self, years: i64, months: i64, days: i64, overflow: Overflow) -> Option<PlainDate>
```

Returns the date `years` years and `months` months from this date, and then `days` days
from there, or `None` when it is outside the range, or when `overflow` is `Reject` and the
day does not exist in the month reached.

#### Details

It is [`PlainDate.checkedAddPeriod`](#PlainDate.impl.checkedAddPeriod) for counts that can have different signs, such as one
month later and one day earlier.

<a id="PlainDate.impl.periodUntil"></a>

### Method `periodUntil`

```silk
pub fn periodUntil(self: Self, other: PlainDate, largest: DateUnit) -> Period
```

Returns the calendar span from this date to `other`, counted in `largest` units first. It
is negative when `other` is earlier, and its time part is empty.

#### Details

With `DateUnit.Year` or `DateUnit.Month`, the result has the most whole months that can be
added to this date without passing `other`, and then the days that are left. With
`DateUnit.Week`, it has whole weeks and days, and with `DateUnit.Day`, only days. Adding
the result to this date with [`PlainDate.addPeriod`](#PlainDate.impl.addPeriod) gives `other`. This is the rule of
ECMAScript Temporal.

#### Gotchas

The span from `other` back to this date is not always the negated result. From
2023-01-29 to 2023-03-01 is 1 month and 1 day, and from 2023-03-01 back to 2023-01-29 is 1
month and 3 days.

<a id="PlainDate.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub fn parse(text: string) -> Result<PlainDate, TimeParseError>
```

Reads a date from ISO 8601 text such as `2026-11-19`.

#### Details

The text is `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYYMMDD`; a year outside 0 to 9999 has a sign and six digits.
A time, a numeric UTC offset, and bracketed annotations can follow, as in
`2026-11-19T17:36:22+01:00[Europe/Rome]`. They are checked and then ignored.

#### Errors

- `TimeParseReason.UnexpectedEnd` or `UnexpectedCharacter` if the text does not have that
  form.
- `TimeParseReason.OutOfRange` if a field names no real value, such as month 13 or February
  30, or the date is outside `-271821-04-19` to `+275760-09-13`.
- `TimeParseReason.UtcNotAllowed` if the text has the UTC designator `Z`.
- `TimeParseReason.UnsupportedCalendar` if a calendar annotation is not `[u-ca=iso8601]`.
- `TimeParseReason.UnknownCriticalAnnotation` if an annotation with an unknown key starts
  with `!`.

#### Details

The text is `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYYMMDD`; a year outside 0 to 9999 has a sign and six digits.
A time, a numeric UTC offset, and bracketed annotations can follow. They are checked and then
ignored.

#### Errors

- `TimeParseReason.UnexpectedEnd` or `UnexpectedCharacter` if the text does not have that

- `TimeParseReason.OutOfRange` if a field names no real value, such as month 13 or February

- `TimeParseReason.UtcNotAllowed` if the text has the UTC designator `Z`.
- `TimeParseReason.UnsupportedCalendar` if a calendar annotation is not `[u-ca=iso8601]`.
- `TimeParseReason.UnknownCriticalAnnotation` if an annotation with an unknown key starts
  with `!`.
